author_role: independent AI research proposal, not human expert endorsement
selection_basis: Named important questions before endpoint selection
Distinct resource coverage rather than raw unknown-pair count
Exact mathematical universe and model conventions
Implementation effort and expected proof tractability excluded from importance ranking

current_domain.demotion_caveat: Complement satellites are not aliases. Background retention preserves inference vocabulary, not all scored endpoint coverage.

candidates.label: QMA(2)
candidates.question: QMA(2) ⊆ QMA? NEXP ⊆ QMA(2)?
candidates.scientific_reason: Adds unentanglement as a distinct verification resource, with optimization and separability connections.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Canonical separation from QMA may have only promise witnesses; specialized short-proof results do not settle this endpoint.
candidates.definition_requirements: Two polynomial-qubit product witnesses; polynomial-time uniform verifier; soundness against all product states; bounded gap.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Strong addition; NEXP containment is faithfully captured by completion. Label QMA comparison as total-restricted.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: QMA(k)=QMA2 for 2≤k≤poly under standard error conventions
implementation_issues: Product-state semantics; amplification and mixtures; no entangled joint witness.

candidates.label: StoqMA
candidates.question: StoqMA ⊆ MA?
candidates.scientific_reason: Connects sign-problem-free Hamiltonians to classical verification and randomness.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: General equality and physical subclass algorithms are different goals; threshold normalization is itself open.
candidates.definition_requirements: Reversible NOT/CNOT/Toffoli verifier, zero/plus ancillas, X-basis output. Union of efficient a(n),b(n) with 1/2≤b<a≤1 and inverse-polynomial gap.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Coherent useful total restriction; canonical promise equality implies it, reverse transfer unproved.
implementation_issues: Do not set soundness 1/3; do not assume standard gap amplification.
The exact soundness b=1/2 boundary has an NP characterization (Liu Corollary 24); no blanket identity across all allowed parameter choices.

candidates.label: QSZK
candidates.question: QSZK ⊆ QMA? QSZK ⊆ BQP?
candidates.scientific_reason: Adds quantum state distinguishability and statistical simulation, with cryptographic consequences.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Canonical complete problems are promised; some cryptographic advances do not decide any inclusion.
candidates.definition_requirements: Quantum interactive proofs with statistical simulation against the intended verifier class; classical descriptions of circuits/states.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Useful total restriction; no automatic converse from a total containment to all promise instances.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Strong addition; match malicious-verifier and honest-verifier equivalence theorem.
implementation_issues: Trace distance, simulator uniformity, auxiliary information, circuit encodings.

candidates.label: QPCP[O(1)]
candidates.question: QMA ⊆ QPCP[O(1)]?
candidates.scientific_reason: The proof-checking quantum PCP conjecture supplies a missing major research target.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Total-language inclusion need not settle the canonical conjecture; Hamiltonian formulations depend on quantum versus classical reductions. One focused conjecture consumes a slot.
candidates.definition_requirements: One polynomial-size quantum proof; polynomial-time uniform verifier; constant proof-qubit queries; fixed bounded error; union over constant query bounds.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Admissible as Tot(QPCP), but lower priority unless incomplete capture is accepted explicitly.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Strong addition after pinning Definition 5 convention.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: QMA ⊆ QPCP is the proof-checking quantum PCP conjecture
implementation_issues: Query semantics and adaptivity; no implicit classical reduction to constant-gap local Hamiltonians.

candidates.label: BPL
candidates.question: BPL ⊆ L?
candidates.scientific_reason: Space-bounded derandomization is not represented by P versus BPP.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: RL offers a competing one-sided formulation; selecting many nearby logspace variants costs breadth.
candidates.definition_requirements: Probabilistic logspace, read-only input, polynomial time, bounded error on all inputs for total track.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Keep classical promise counterpart explicit when used as a quantum-space anchor.
implementation_issues: Runtime convention and read-only random-bit access.

candidates.label: BQL
candidates.question: BQL ⊆ BPL? BQL ⊆ L? NL ⊆ BQL?
candidates.scientific_reason: Quantum space is distinct from time-bounded BQP; recent natural total-language examples support the bridge.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Many complete linear-algebra problems are promised, and this slot competes with BPL/UL or verification variants.
candidates.definition_requirements: Polynomial time, logarithmic total workspace including classical control, read-only classical input, bounded error.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Strong addition where space breadth is desired; total example in Apers–Edenhofer Theorem 4.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Strong alternative; unitary and general versions are equivalent in the specified resource model.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: BQL=unitary BQL under the measurement-elimination theorem
implementation_issues: Count classical control; do not use the time-only deferred-measurement argument.

candidates.label: QMA₁
candidates.question: QMA ⊆ QMA1?
candidates.scientific_reason: Perfect completeness is a longstanding basic question and has natural quantum satisfiability complete problems.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: A fixed-gate version is an exact convention, not a theorem that all universal gate sets agree; the slot may buy less breadth than QSZK or QMA2.
candidates.definition_requirements: Fixed exact gate set such as H,T,CNOT; acceptance exactly one for yes; bounded soundness for no.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Captures that fixed-gate total question; cannot advertise all canonical promise/gate formulations without a transfer theorem.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Strong alternative if exact gates are in the task specification.
implementation_issues: Approximate gate compilation cannot preserve exact completeness; post-cutoff claims excluded.

candidates.label: NISZK
candidates.question: SZK ⊆ NISZK?
candidates.scientific_reason: Asks whether interaction is necessary for statistical zero knowledge.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Common random string and promise conventions are essential; less coverage of quantum computation than a QSZK slot.
candidates.definition_requirements: One proof relative to a common random string; statistical simulation; specify reuse and verifier model.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Coherent total restriction; do not automatically lift its equality to all promise problems.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: Promise NISZK complement closure iff promise NISZK=SZK
implementation_issues: No plain-model substitution; distinguish computational NIZK.

candidates.label: QIP(2)
candidates.question: QIP2 ⊆ QMA? PSPACE ⊆ QIP2?
candidates.scientific_reason: Represents the unresolved two-message position between witnesses and full interaction.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: One can reasonably prefer a different field to a second quantum interaction endpoint.
candidates.definition_requirements: Verifier sends a quantum message, prover applies arbitrary channel and replies, verifier measures; bounded gap.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Useful total model; PSPACE containment has a completion transfer, separation from QMA may not.
implementation_issues: Channels, private registers, message count rather than ambiguous round count.

candidates.label: BQP/qpoly and BQP/poly
candidates.question: BQP/qpoly ⊆ BQP/poly?
candidates.scientific_reason: Tests whether quantum advice is more powerful than classical advice.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Direct representation costs two endpoints; a broad roster has stronger single-slot omissions.
candidates.definition_requirements: Advice depends only on input length; polynomial classical bits or qubits; uniform polynomial-time quantum computation otherwise.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Mathematically legitimate nonuniform total classes; do not confuse arbitrary advice with computable advice.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Promise versions require separate typing and domain conventions.
implementation_issues: 2026 classical-oracle separation is not ordinary separation.

candidates.label: DQC1 / BQ1P
candidates.question: Does one-clean-qubit computation exceed classical randomized computation?
candidates.scientific_reason: A physically distinct restricted quantum model with trace-estimation problems.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: DQC1 does not denote one universally interchangeable controller/gap model; select a definition before adding edges.
candidates.definition_requirements: One pure qubit, maximally mixed remainder, no free reset, final measurement; fix classical controller and input access.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Possible, using an explicit total-language BQ1P-style convention or another named choice.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Promise trace estimation is natural; resource conventions still matter.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: Shepherd model has no immediate P containment from its definition
implementation_issues: Logspace uniform input-bit control versus polynomial-time input-dependent generation; gap amplification.

candidates.label: EQP and ZQP
candidates.question: BQP ⊆ ZQP? ZQP ⊆ EQP?
candidates.scientific_reason: Exposes exact and zero-error quantum computation.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Gate and expected-time conventions add sensitivity; surveyed proof and space questions have stronger broad-roster claims.
candidates.definition_requirements: Exact acceptance versus zero error with explicit runtime and failure conventions; fixed gates.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Possible total endpoints, not currently preferred over major missing resources.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Specify promises and reject silent expected-time/bounded-time identification.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: EQP ⊆ bounded-error quantum computation under matching model
implementation_issues: Exact gates; expected-time versus failure-symbol variants.

candidates.label: UniqueQMA / UQMA
candidates.question: Does quantum verification admit a useful uniqueness reduction?
candidates.scientific_reason: Quantum analogue of the isolation/unique-witness program.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: The central result may be a randomized promise reduction, not a class inclusion; adding a node can fail to score the intended advance.
candidates.definition_requirements: Specify unique accepting state/subspace and spectral soundness, rather than merely a unique classical string.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Total restriction may miss the isolation question.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Consider only with a precisely chosen inclusion or reduction task type.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: No ordinary QMA=UQMA inferred from a randomized reduction alone

candidates.label: QAM and public-coin quantum variants
candidates.question: How much does public-coin quantum interaction add?
candidates.scientific_reason: Separates communication resources and public randomness.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Many incompatible quantum/classical message variants; QIP2 is a cleaner single representative for a broad roster.
candidates.definition_requirements: Fix whether coins/messages are classical, quantum, or half-EPR states, plus message order.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Only after exact total model selection.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: An interaction-specialized roster can justify these instead of QIP2.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: Do not conflate QAM, qqQAM, QIP2
implementation_issues: Different message alphabets and public-coin meanings.

candidates.label: Quantum polynomial hierarchies
candidates.question: Do quantum alternation hierarchies collapse?
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Several inequivalent hierarchies; one unnamed QPH endpoint cannot stand for all.
candidates.definition_requirements: Fix classical/quantum quantifiers, entanglement permissions and consistency promises.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Research-specific alternative after exact target selection.
implementation_issues: Alternating quantum witnesses and incompatible definitions.

candidates.label: QNC and shallow-quantum classes
candidates.question: Can shallow quantum circuits perform tasks beyond shallow classical circuits?
candidates.scientific_reason: Quantum parallelism and geometry are distinct resources.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Classical preprocessing, fanout, adaptivity and geometry can dominate the comparison; proof/space omissions presently have clearer endpoints.
candidates.definition_requirements: Fix uniformity, gate fan-in, geometry, depth, measurements and classical control.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Possible total class with full model declaration.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Promise or sampling variants require own types.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: No generic QNC=NC or inclusion imported by analogy
implementation_issues: Depth-preserving compilation and classical control costs.

candidates.label: PostBPP / BPPpath
candidates.question: How does classical postselection compare with BQP or counting?
candidates.scientific_reason: A natural classical counterpart to quantum postselection.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: A counting-heavy roster already represents related resources; this competes with entirely absent space or physical models.
candidates.definition_requirements: Condition on a nonzero postselection event; require conditional bounded error; explicit uniformity.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Specify behavior and nonzero probability throughout the promise.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: PostBQP is already PP, so do not add both as distinct scored names
implementation_issues: No zero-probability conditioning or uncomputable probabilities.

candidates.label: SampBPP and SampBQP
candidates.question: Can efficient quantum sampling be classically simulated?
candidates.scientific_reason: Captures a central version of efficient quantum advantage that decision classes need not settle.
candidates.strongest_counterargument: Costs another object type and at least two endpoints; exact/approximate sampling and error metrics differ.
candidates.definition_requirements: Uniform samplers for distribution families, total variation or specified metric, accuracy parameter and runtime convention.
candidates.total_language_recommendation: Out of scope; do not rename samplers as languages.
candidates.typed_track_recommendation: Strong separate-track case if the user authorizes sampling.
known_anchors_for_later_audit: Sampling-search equivalence is not BPP=BQP for decision classes
implementation_issues: Approximation accuracy; task size; classical input and output encodings.

notes: A total-to-promise restriction/completion theorem is a typed transfer, not equality of objects.
Changing every old endpoint to a promise class requires re-auditing counting, unambiguity, advice and intersections.
A sampling track is another universe and is not authorized by mere permission for promises.
Do not hide duplicated total/promise classes when reporting the 40–50 endpoint count.

promise_transfer.statement: C⊆D for promise classes implies Tot(C)⊆Tot(D); Tot(C)⊄Tot(D) implies C⊄D.
promise_transfer.proof: A total language is the promise pair (L, complement L). The same verifier witnesses inclusion or separation.

promise_transfer.statement: Promise separation need not yield a total-language witness; total inclusion need not cover all promise problems.
promise_transfer.proof: Arbitrary behavior outside the promise can include intermediate probabilities and may not admit a total gap-preserving completion.

promise_transfer.statement: Every P, NP, PSPACE or NEXP promise problem has a total completion in the same resource class.
promise_transfer.proof: Use the deterministic acceptance language, or the existential acceptance language of the nondeterministic machine, including behavior off promise. Global resource bounds remain unchanged.
Complete the NEXP promise problem, apply the total inclusion, then restrict the resulting QMA2 verifier to the original promise.

open_problem_coverage.question: P=BPP?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Directly represented; does not by itself certify every PromiseBPP problem has a P solution.

open_problem_coverage.question: L=BPL?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Directly represented by new total BPL endpoint.

open_problem_coverage.question: BQL=BPL?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Total equality has direct meaning; promise equality is stronger without a completion proof.

open_problem_coverage.question: BQP=BPP?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Current total statement meaningful; does not encompass all promise or sampling advantage.

open_problem_coverage.question: QMA=QCMA?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Promise inclusion implies total inclusion; a promise separation may have no total-language witness.

open_problem_coverage.question: QMA2=QMA?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Adding total QMA2 captures total question, not every canonical promise separation.

open_problem_coverage.question: QMA2=NEXP?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: NEXP completion proves total NEXP⊆total QMA2 suffices for canonical inclusion; upper bound already known.

open_problem_coverage.question: QMA=QMA1?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: A fixed-gate total inclusion is only that convention and universe; no blanket gate/promise equivalence.

open_problem_coverage.question: StoqMA=MA?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Total restriction useful; canonical equality not recovered automatically from total equality.

open_problem_coverage.question: QMA=QPCP[O(1)]?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Total QPCP inclusion is a weaker target; quantum-versus-classical reductions remain a separate caveat.

open_problem_coverage.question: QSZK⊆QMA?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Promise positive result transfers; total separation transfers; converse directions not assumed.

open_problem_coverage.question: SZK=NISZK?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Promise equivalences and black-box barriers must not silently be applied as total equalities/separations.

open_problem_coverage.question: QIP2=QMA? QIP2=PSPACE?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: PSPACE-source inclusion has completion transfer; QIP2-source separation/inclusion has usual promise caveat.

open_problem_coverage.question: BQP/qpoly=BQP/poly?
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Real ordinary question; the 2026 oracle result gives no ordinary answer.

open_problem_coverage.question: Efficient algorithm for a restricted Hamiltonian family
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: Can be important while implying no equality between broad classes.

open_problem_coverage.question: Classical or quantum oracle separates quantum proof classes
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: No ordinary inclusion/separation follows without additional argument.

open_problem_coverage.question: Shorter proofs, sharper gaps, faster simulation, restricted circuit lower bounds
open_problem_coverage.total_transfer: May leave all polynomial-union class labels unchanged.
